_doc: #767 THE ONE DECLARATION of Cloud-Lib-Calc's native engine: libqalculate and everything it links, built from pinned upstream source into ONE self-contained JNI library per ABI (libqalc.so: qalc_core + qalc_jni + static libqalculate, libxml2, MPFR, GMP, libc++). PRODUCER: ship-lib-calc-native.yml -> native/publish-qalc.sh -> native/build-qalc.sh, which also builds the same core for the CI host and runs native/golden.tsv and libqalculate's own test suite against it before anything is published. CONSUMER: build.gradle stages the pinned asset as jniLibs/<abi>/libqalc.so after a sha256 check, and never builds C++ itself, so a red native build cannot stop a Cloud Libs publish (the firestack-aar split, ship-firestack-aar.yml). Adopting a build is a deliberate edit of data/qalc-pin.json made after reading the release notes, never automatic.
_doc_why_qalculate: libqalculate is the engine behind Qalculate! (GPL-2.0-or-later): symbolic and numeric evaluation, ~4000 units with dimension checking, physical constants (CODATA), currencies, date/time arithmetic, bitwise and base conversion, finance functions (pmt/fv/pv/nper), calculus (diff/integrate/solve/factor) and plot sampling, with its definitions compiled into the library (--enable-compiled-definitions) so nothing is unpacked at runtime. numbat (MIT/Apache-2.0) was considered for 'dimension-safe' expressions and NOT adopted: qalculate's unit arithmetic is already dimension-aware ('500 W * 2 h to kWh' = 1 kWh is a golden row) and it covers every mode the app has, so numbat would be a second engine with a second unit table for one overlapping feature.

build._doc_sources: Release tarballs, sha256-pinned (verified by downloading each one, 2026-10-02). build-qalc.sh builds them in `order`, each into one install prefix per target, as static PIC archives. `configure` applies to every target; `android` and `host` are appended for that kind of target only.

gmp._doc_configure: --disable-assembly: GMP's hand-written asm is the least portable part of it across NDK clang versions, and a calculator's numbers are small; the C fallback is correct everywhere.

libxml2._doc_configure: libqalculate only parses its own UTF-8 definitions with it: no Python binding, no compression, no iconv/ICU (UTF-8 is native to libxml2), no network, no dlopen'd modules.

libqalculate._doc_configure: Definitions compiled in. No libcurl: exchange rates are downloaded by the engine's Kotlin side through Android's resolver (so the SuperApp's DNS menu applies, #741) into the files libqalculate reads, then reloaded. No ICU (case-insensitive non-ASCII names only), no gnuplot/popen, no insecure command() function, no gettext. The host build adds the qalc text port and its unit-test runner so `make check` runs libqalculate's own tests/*.batch against these exact flags.

build._doc_ndk: The NDK the Android targets are compiled with, and the API level the binary may assume (the lib APKs' min_sdk). Static libc++ is linked in, so the APK's own NDK version is irrelevant to this .so.
build._doc_soname: The one file per ABI, loaded by QalcNative.kt with System.loadLibrary("qalc"). Its only NEEDED entries may be the platform libraries in allowed_needed; anything else would be a library the APK does not carry.
build._doc_page_size: 16 KB ELF alignment so the library loads on 16 KB-page devices (Android 15+); 4 KB-page devices load it unchanged.

publish._doc: Where publish-qalc.sh puts a build: its own immutable tag per publish (prefix + UTC timestamp), one asset per ABI because the bytes are per ABI. What the Cloud Libs build USES is data/qalc-pin.json, a separate file so that adopting a build does not re-trigger the builder.
